newsitem.title: FRANCE: Olympic signs contract for 2 Airbus A340s.
newsitem.headline: Olympic signs contract for 2 Airbus A340s.

text.p: Greek state-owned carrier Olympic Airlines has signed a contract to buy two Airbus A340-300 passenger jets, Airbus Industrie said on Tuesday.
Olympic has also taken options for two more A340 planes and plans to operate a fleet of six A340s by 2000, Airbus said in a statement.

The purchase had previously been authorised by transport and communications minister Haris Kastanidis, on the recommendation of the Greek state audit council. The purchase decision had already been announced.

Olympic will take delivery of the four-engined widebody aircraft starting in the third quarter of 1998, Airbus said The planes will be powered by CFM56 engines from CFM International and will have a two-class layout, with 32 passengers in business and 267 in economy class.
CFMI is a joint venture between General Electric Co and French state-owned Snecma.
Catalogue price for the A340 is around $124 million.
Airbus is a consortium made up of France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa).
